newsitem.title: UK: Union sees strike vote from BA ground staff.
newsitem.headline: Union sees strike vote from BA ground staff.

text.p: A ballot of British Airways Plc ground crew staff is expected to show overwhelming support for strike action, the Transport & General Workers Union (T&G) said on Monday.
George Wright of the T&G told BBC radio that if the vote was in favour of strike action, the union would meet with staff representatives on Tuesday to discuss the next step.
The result of the ballot is due later on Monday, and under UK law, a union must give seven days notice of strike action to employers.

British Airways cabin crew last week voted overwhelmingly for action in a separate dispute over pay -- the ground staff dispute is over BA plans to sell off its catering division as part of restructuring plans to save one billion pounds by the end of the century.

BA has reacted strongly to the strike threat, saying over the weekend that striking staff could be sacked or sued for damages. The company also has contingency plans to bus in non-striking employees and take on staff to fill the jobs of striking staff.
A meeting of the T&G and representatives of the cabin crew who voted for action was set for Monday.
